edges.glue: create the user namespace: the room gets its own uid table
edges.name: unshare_user

edges.glue: map inner uid (param uid) to the caller's uid: inside, we are root
edges.name: write_uid_map

edges.glue: create the mount namespace: mounts made here stay inside the room
edges.name: unshare_mount

edges.glue: the room gets its own network namespace (its own interfaces, routes and sockets); loopback is brought up so 127.0.0.1 works inside
edges.name: unshare_net

edges.glue: child becomes pid 1 of a new pid namespace; parent waits and propagates the exit code
edges.name: unshare_pid

edges.glue: stop mount propagation leaking out of the room
edges.name: mount_private_root

edges.glue: the rootfs becomes a mount point, so chroot has a clean tree
edges.name: bind_rootfs

edges.glue: a fresh /proc matching the (possibly new) pid namespace
edges.name: mount_proc

edges.glue: host device nodes (param devices, or --device PATH, repeatable) are bind-mounted into rootfs/dev: the room sees exactly the devices it is given, no others. This is how a GPU is handed in (e.g. /dev/nvidia0, /dev/nvidiactl, /dev/nvidia-uvm)
edges.name: bind_device

edges.glue: cross the threshold: / is now the rootfs
edges.name: chroot_rootfs

edges.glue: chroot leaves cwd outside; step into the room's workdir
edges.name: chdir_work

edges.glue: pin the command to the CPUs named by param cpus / --cpus (list like 0, 0-1, 0,2): a device-side restriction done with sched_setaffinity, no cgroup delegation needed
edges.name: pin_cpus

edges.glue: the pole's algorithm runs: the command replaces this process
edges.name: exec_cmd

pole.description: bwrap rewritten in Link edge notation: the pole is the room (an isolated process environment); the builder generates the edges (named syscall steps) that glue the outside of the room to its inside.

inputs.env: not inherited; the edge exec_cmd installs a minimal generated env (PATH, HOME, TERM)

pole.name: lwrap

outputs.exit: the command's exit code, propagated (also through the unshare_pid fork)
outputs.stderr: the command's stderr; lwrap's own edge failures are named on stderr
